name: Polonnaruwa
line: A medieval royal city, flat enough to see by bicycle.

image.alt: The carved moonstone and steps of the Polonnaruwa Vatadage at dusk

summary: The island’s medieval capital, spread through shady parkland. We see it by bicycle, one ruin at a time.

intro.heading: A city you can cycle.
paragraphs: Polonnaruwa was the royal capital around nine hundred years ago. Its palaces, temples and stupas are spread over several kilometres of flat, shaded parkland beside a huge reservoir built by King Parakramabahu.
It is an hour from Sigiriya, so we treat it as a day out. Bicycles and a guide at the gate, an early start, and the stone Buddhas of the Gal Vihara saved for last.

mapCaption: In the east of the Cultural Triangle. The other dots are the places we pair it with.

doing.lede: Polonnaruwa is a morning on two wheels. These are the things we build the day around.

items.title: The ruins by bicycle
items.body: Flat paths, shade most of the way, and a guide riding with you. We stop at the Quadrangle, the royal palace and the lotus pond.

items.title: The Gal Vihara
items.body: Four Buddhas cut into a single granite face, one of them fourteen metres long and lying down. The finest carving on the island.

items.title: The reservoir at dusk
items.body: Parakrama Samudra is big enough to look like a lake. Families come down to the bund to swim and watch the light go.

items.title: Elephants at Minneriya
items.body: The national park is half an hour away. From July to September the gathering there is one of the great wildlife sights of Asia.

gallery.alt: Elephants grazing on open grassland at Minneriya
Stone ruins among the trees at Polonnaruwa

season: Polonnaruwa follows the Cultural Triangle: dry for most of the year and at its best from February to April. The Minneriya gathering peaks in August and September, as the reservoir shrinks.
ctaBody: Tell us your dates and we will fit it in, with the bicycles waiting at the gate.
